name: Eculizumab
route_note: IV infusion weekly for induction, then every 2 weeks
owner: AstraZeneca (Alexion); biosimilars from Amgen and Samsung Bioepis

discovery.note: Humanised antibody with a hybrid IgG2/IgG4 constant region that binds complement component C5.

tagline: First complement inhibitor, transforming PNH and atypical HUS
summary: Eculizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that blocks complement protein C5, preventing formation of the membrane attack complex. It was the first approved complement inhibitor and is used for paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome, generalised myasthenia gravis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
mechanism: Eculizumab binds C5 and prevents its cleavage by C5 convertase into C5a, a potent anaphylatoxin, and C5b, which initiates assembly of the C5b-9 membrane attack complex.

In PNH, red cells lacking the complement regulators CD55 and CD59 are lysed by the membrane attack complex; blocking C5 stops intravascular haemolysis. Terminal complement blockade also impairs killing of Neisseria, causing a high risk of meningococcal infection.
uses: Generalised myasthenia gravis with anti-AChR antibodies

history.title: TRIUMPH
history.detail: Phase 3 TRIUMPH trial in PNH shows reduced haemolysis and transfusion needs.

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in March (US) and June (EU) for PNH.

history.title: Atypical HUS
history.detail: Approved for atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome.

history.title: Ravulizumab
history.detail: Alexion's longer-acting successor, ravulizumab, is approved for PNH.

history.title: NMOSD
history.detail: Approved for anti-AQP4-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

history.title: AstraZeneca acquisition
history.detail: AstraZeneca completes its $39 billion acquisition of Alexion.

history.title: Biosimilars
history.detail: FDA approves the first eculizumab biosimilars, Bkemv and Epysqli.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: Other encapsulated bacterial infections (including disseminated gonococcal infection)
Haemolysis or thrombotic microangiopathy after discontinuation
safety.boxed_warning: Life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections; vaccinate at least 2 weeks before treatment; available only through a REMS programme.

facts: For years Soliris was among the most expensive drugs in the world, at several hundred thousand US dollars per year.
Meningococcal risk persists despite vaccination, so some patients also receive prophylactic antibiotics.
